# DeskUtils 0.1.8
DeskUtils 0.1.8 rebuilds onboarding around guided feature demos, replaces the inert Pro locks with one shared upgrade panel, and gives Full Annotate backgrounds and pinned screenshots a significant upgrade.
## What's New
- **New onboarding** — a seven-page flow with looping, muted video demos for Quick Ring, Screenshot, Clipboard, Capture Text, and more. Every feature page has an animated fallback when a demo is unavailable, **Skip** jumps to the end, and the final page offers Accessibility and Screen Recording access without making them mandatory. Launch at Login is set on the last page. Replay it from **Settings → General → Help → Restart**. - **Shared Pro upgrade panel** — every Pro-gated action (menu bar, Settings, Quick Ring, global shortcuts) now opens one consistent panel that names the feature being used, lists the Pro benefits, and offers a single **Get DeskUtils Pro** button. Locked items stay clickable instead of showing a static lock badge. - **Annotate background sidebar** — open it with the toolbar `rectangle.on.rectangle` button or ⌘B to style the canvas behind your screenshot. Choose gradients, five bundled wallpapers plus your own, blurred backgrounds, or solid colors, then tune padding, shadow, corners, aspect ratio, and alignment. Backgrounds are saved with the document and restored when you reopen it. - **Pinned screenshot windows** — pinned images now show **Close**, **Edit**, **Zoom**, **Lock**, and a drag handle on hover. Zoom with the percentage pill, scroll wheel, or pinch; lock the window to click through to apps underneath; drag the pin into another app as a file; and jump straight to Full Annotate with edits reflected in place.
## Improvements
- The curved arrow tool now has a control handle, so you can adjust its curvature after drawing. - Refined the Quick Ring radial menu: a softer glass background with a gradient rim, subtler slot fills, and active tools marked by a green icon instead of a small dot. The live panel and Settings preview share the same rendering. - External Display Only now appears in the menu as a session section with an inline on/off toggle, and keeps its explicit retry action when recovery fails.
## Fixes
- Corrected canvas background rendering and constrained backgrounds to the annotation canvas. - Annotation selection chrome is now shape-specific and matches the selected tool. - Fixed pinned screenshot windows drifting out of sync: source URLs stay current, Quick Access preview updates are gated by the editor's render generation, and focus and save state stay consistent. - Aligned and centered the Pro upgrade benefits with the panel subtitle, and fixed a race that could dismiss the panel right after it opened. - Onboarding now shows the display dimming tool.
## Notes
- Build 12. - The annotate wallpaper library ships five default wallpapers; custom wallpapers you add are stored as bookmarks and stay on your Mac. - Pinned windows and Full Annotate follow your system Reduce Motion setting. - Onboarding and upgrade interactions are covered by the existing opt-out anonymous analytics, configurable in **About → Privacy**. - Requires macOS 15.2 or later.

# DeskUtils 0.1.7
DeskUtils 0.1.7 introduces Quick Ring for fast access to your tools, improves clipboard navigation and search, and makes screenshot copying work better with web apps.
## What's New
- **Quick Ring** — press Command twice to open a radial menu with eight tool slots. Click an action, or hold the second Command press, move toward an action, and release to run it. - Configure Quick Ring in **Settings → Quick Ring**, including an alternate shortcut, placement at the pointer or screen center, and haptic feedback. DeskUtils Pro lets you rearrange slots and change their actions. - **Launch at Login** is now available during onboarding, so you can choose to start DeskUtils automatically when you log in.
## Improvements
- Smoother keyboard navigation and more responsive search in Clipboard Manager, especially with larger histories. - Screenshot History now offers explicit **Copy Image** and **Copy File** actions. Copy a single screenshot as an image for pasting into apps, or copy files for Finder and attachment fields. Multiple screenshots can be copied together as files. - More balanced spacing for the CPU, memory, and disk gauges in the menu bar popover.
## Fixes
- Screenshots copied from Quick Access and Screenshot History now use image clipboard formats that web apps such as Excel Online can accept. - Fixed typing from the clipboard list being incorrectly handled as a filter search action.
## Notes
- Build 11. - Quick Ring requires Accessibility permission. Individual actions retain their existing permission and Pro requirements. - Requires macOS 15.2 or later.
